title: Add cost-bounded Linux CI for Orbit
description: Orbit is private and currently has no .github directory, workflow files, or GitHub Actions runs. Add the smallest automatic CI guard for the current Rust verification surface while preventing unexpected paid runner usage and unnecessary depletion of the private-repository minute allowance. This is repository tooling and changes no ORB-C product contract.
design:
Create one GitHub Actions workflow for the existing private repository. Run it automatically only for pushes to edge that touch Rust, Cargo, toolchain, test, or workflow surfaces, plus workflow_dispatch for deliberate reruns. Use one standard Ubuntu job and run the canonical Rust checks sequentially so compilation work is reused within the job:

- cargo fmt --check
- cargo check --locked
- cargo test --locked
- cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings

Set explicit read-only GITHUB_TOKEN permissions, pin every referenced action to a verified full commit SHA, cap the job at 10 minutes, and cancel superseded edge runs with a concurrency group. Log rustc and cargo versions. Do not add a matrix, macOS or Windows runner, larger runner, schedule, nightly build, artifact upload, cache, coverage service, release step, secret, self-hosted runner, or third-party setup action. Do not make the repository public as part of this bead.

Before enabling the workflow, confirm an Actions budget of $0 with stop-usage enabled and billing alerts for the repository or owning account. If repository-scoped budget control is unavailable to the implementing agent, stop and ask the user to configure or confirm it; do not silently enable paid overage. A workflow cannot enforce the account budget itself.

No crate or manifest change is expected. If CI requires a new direct dependency, Cargo feature, toolchain policy, cache, service, or non-GitHub action, stop for the applicable crate or scope decision. The portability disposition is neutral: Linux CI verifies the authorized Linux-first slice and creates no macOS support promise.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Before editing workflow or documentation files, the bead has an Execution baseline and a pre-implementation Reference gate. It explicitly routes no product contract and records the portability disposition as neutral.
2. Exactly one repository workflow is added. It runs on workflow_dispatch and on pushes to edge only when Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, Rust source, tests, build.rs, Rust toolchain files, or the workflow itself changes. Documentation-only and Beads-only pushes do not consume a run.
3. The workflow contains one standard Ubuntu job. It has a 10-minute timeout and concurrency cancellation for superseded edge revisions.
4. GITHUB_TOKEN permissions are explicitly read-only at the narrowest useful level. Every external action is GitHub-owned, source-reviewed for the used behavior, and pinned to a verified full commit SHA.
5. The job logs toolchain versions and runs cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, and cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings. All commands exit 0 on the accepted edge revision.
6. The workflow has no OS, Rust-version, feature, or target matrix; no macOS, Windows, larger, or self-hosted runner; no schedule; no cache; no uploaded artifact; no coverage or release service; and no secret or write permission.
7. Before the first hosted run, a $0 GitHub Actions budget with stop-usage enabled and billing alerts is confirmed for the applicable repository or account. If this cannot be verified or requires user billing access, implementation stops before enabling automatic runs and gives the user exact confirmation steps.
8. One cold hosted run succeeds within the timeout. Closure records its URL, elapsed time, billable minutes reported by GitHub, runner type, and the resulting expected monthly-minute envelope for the observed push cadence.
9. README documentation states what triggers CI, what it checks, how to dispatch it manually, and the cost ceiling. README LOC accounting changes only if required by its actual scorecard rules. CHANGELOG.md is not changed because this bead changes no runtime or consumer contract.
10. No Cargo dependency, feature, product behavior, ORB-C entry, public visibility, branch topology, or macOS support commitment changes.
11. The closure notes tell orb-9o6 to extend this established workflow with its governance command after that command exists; this bead does not pull the deferred governance checker forward.
notes:
Evidence:

- The repository has no .github directory or workflow in HEAD, and gh run list for luccahuguet/orbit returned no runs on 2026-08-03.
- GitHub reports luccahuguet/orbit as PRIVATE with edge as its default branch.
- AGENTS.md and README.md define the current Rust verification surface and the Linux-first scope.

Reference routing for the mandatory pre-implementation Reference gate:

Required before code:
- The exact AGENTS.md, README.md, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, and current GitHub repository visibility and Actions settings.
- GitHub Actions billing: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions
- GitHub budgets and alerts: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/budgets-and-alerts
- Workflow syntax for path filters, permissions, concurrency, and timeout-minutes: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax
- GitHub secure-use guidance for least privilege and immutable action pinning: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use

Conditional on a named failure:
- GitHub-hosted runner image documentation only if the standard Ubuntu image lacks the existing stable Rust requirements or a canonical command fails because of runner contents.
- Cache research only if a measured cold run exceeds the 10-minute ceiling; stop before adding caching or storage usage.

Comparison only:
- Current local verification duration and one cold GitHub-hosted run are measurements, not architecture references.

Rejected scope:
- Making Orbit public merely to obtain free Actions minutes.
- Self-hosted infrastructure, matrices, cross-platform CI, nightly or scheduled work, coverage, releases, artifacts, caches, larger runners, and paid overage.
- Moving orb-9o6 earlier or pretending CI mechanically validates human governance judgments.

Maintenance:
- Public visibility remains a separate product and publication decision.
- The $0 budget is the hard financial boundary; path filters, one job, timeouts, and cancellation preserve included minutes.
- Once orb-9o6 provides its repository-local governance command, that bead should add the command to this workflow and expand path triggers only for the metadata it actually checks.

title: Automate the machine-checkable governance invariants
description: After the Orbit convergence proof and before Venus implementation, add the smallest repository-local check for governance invariants that can be verified mechanically. The check prevents contract, proof, crate-decision, and Bead metadata drift without pretending to validate human judgment.

Start only after orb-bi4.3 so the checker is derived from two real implementation slices, then complete it before orb-bi4.4 creates cross-repository consumer work. Choose the smallest implementation using the existing toolchain and no new direct crate unless a separate Crate gate proves otherwise. Validate AGENTS.md, docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/CRATES.md, and Beads exports only where the invariant is mechanically knowable. Do not claim to prove that an agent actually read a reference, exercised good judgment, or received user approval when those facts require human evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The Bead records that it changes no product contract and starts from an Execution baseline.
2. The implementation documents the exact invariants it can prove and the governance judgments it deliberately cannot automate.
3. One repository command detects duplicate or malformed ORB-C IDs, unknown contract references, invalid contract statuses, and Proved entries without an immutable proof commit and canonical check.
4. The command detects product implementation Beads without known contract routing or an explicit non-product declaration, and closed implementation Beads missing required gate, closure-evidence, contract-update, or crate-decision markers.
5. Explicit Protocol exception records remain visible and do not get misreported as successful gates.
6. Selected direct or architecture-shaping crate decisions must name exact versions or commits, alternatives, and an evidence Bead; planned and candidate entries remain distinguishable from accepted choices.
7. Focused checks exercise representative valid and invalid metadata without large generated fixtures or tests of prose trivia.

9. No new direct crate is preferred. Any proposed dependency passes the Crate gate before manifest edits.
10. The result records owned LOC, dependency footprint, limitations, and exact verification commands.
11. A pre-implementation Reference gate classifies repository and tool references, explicitly recording that no external reference is required when that is the evidence-backed conclusion.
12. The checker detects product implementation Beads whose closure evidence lacks one of the allowed portability dispositions: neutral, isolated platform dependency, or macOS blocker.
13. Because orb-49h establishes the sole CI workflow first, add the governance command to that same job and extend path filters only to the governed metadata; do not add another workflow, job, or hosted run for the checker.
notes:
Sequencing decision: this checker is intentionally deferred until orb-bi4.3 has completed, then blocks orb-bi4.4. That provides two implementation slices for designing useful checks while enforcing the workflow before Venus becomes a separate contract consumer. It is not a substitute for the execution baseline, reference research, crate comparison, user scope decisions, or exception approval.

Dependency clarification: orb-49h must establish the one cost-bounded workflow before this bead. This bead then extends that workflow in place after orb-bi4.3, preserving the one-job cost and ownership boundary.

title: Prove Orbit as the durable terminal runtime beneath Venus
description: Determine whether a small Rust and libghostty runtime can replace the PTY and session-lifetime role that Zellij provides in the current Mars and Zellij chain while supporting the greenfield Venus graphical client. The authorized experiment is Linux-only, local, one-session, and one-active-client. Either a go or no-go result completes the architectural experiment.
design: docs/RATIONALE.md records the origin, ownership hypothesis, tradeoffs, and stop criteria. docs/REFERENCES.md maps prior art to the slice where it can answer a concrete question. Each implementation bead performs that source review just in time and records the release or commit studied, the contract or failure mode extracted, and the surrounding scope rejected. Venus is the permanent name of the greenfield graphical client; Mars remains the existing product while it is supported, and Mars and Mars Next remain behavioral references only. The orb-bi4.1 decision makes Orbit the sole owner of PTY and libghostty terminal state. Clients receive host-authored structured presentation frames and send semantic input; they do not reconstruct terminal state from Formatter output or raw PTY tails. The boundary must preserve a path to rich terminal presentation and, after separate graduation and scope decisions, host-owned durable workspace topology for native, web, or mobile clients. The authorized experiment itself remains Linux-only, local, one-session, and one-active-client. `orb-bi4.3` is the repository boundary gate. Orbit remains one package and binary through that headless proof. If the gate passes, create the private `luccahuguet/venus` repository before `orb-bi4.4`; graphical Venus code does not enter Orbit. The proven structured presentation contract is the cross-repository boundary. The naming and long-term architecture decisions do not authorize multiplayer, remote transport, layouts, tabs, plugins, a configuration framework, daemon-restart persistence, or unapproved libghostty forks or wrappers in the initial experiment.

2. orb-bi4.8 records an explicit user go or no-go decision for the Venus and Orbit direction.
3. On a go decision, orb-bi4.7 records the sequencing and ownership of post-graduation workspace and client expansions before implementation planning. On a no-go decision, orb-bi4.7 closes as not applicable.
4. No known P0 or P1 correctness risk remains unrecorded.

7. The final plan treats Venus as distinct from Mars and does not change the current Mars and Zellij default without a separate promotion decision.
8. The experiment proves one authoritative terminal with rich structured presentation rather than a text-grid-only, Formatter-checkpoint, or raw-tail replication ceiling.
9. If orb-bi4.3 passes, orb-bi4.4 begins in the private luccahuguet/venus repository and no graphical Venus code enters Orbit.

title: Prove the libghostty attachment model
description: Answer the highest-risk question before building runtime architecture: can the released libghostty-vt Rust API support one headless authoritative terminal and reconstruct a second terminal that continues correctly from an ordered PTY tail?
design: Use the current released libghostty-vt crate and record the exact version and source. Start by reproducing the zmx-style VT bootstrap through the public Formatter and FormatterOptions APIs because the current Rust binding exposes terminal modes and other reconstruction options. Compare direct state export and import only if the current source exposes it; use bounded checkpoint plus raw replay only as a fallback, and reject unbounded history replay. Account for the unstable API, single-thread ownership of !Send and !Sync terminal objects, terminal-generated PTY responses, and the boundary between semantic input events and encoded bytes. Only Orbit may answer terminal queries back to the PTY. Test hidden state that can alter future bytes, including cursor and keyboard modes, pending wrap, alternate and inactive screens, tab stops, character sets, palette and hyperlinks, scrollback required for future resize, and a parser between escape-sequence bytes. Stop for a user decision before adding a fork, compatibility layer, substantial wrapper, or alternative engine.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A minimal Linux Rust proof builds against a recorded released libghostty-vt version with the real feature enabled by default.
2. The proof feeds deterministic VT input into authoritative state and reconstructs a second terminal through the public VT formatter, or records a reproducible reason that strategy fails before trying a fallback.
3. A distinguishing future tail produces equivalent semantic behavior, including hidden modes rather than only equal visible cells.
4. The proof covers attachment while the alternate screen is active followed by exit to the primary screen, and attachment at split points inside escape, UTF-8, and APC or graphics sequences.
5. The result states which active and inactive screen, scrollback, mode, parser, effect, input-encoding, palette, hyperlink, and image state the strategy preserves or loses.
6. The result records thread ownership, required callbacks, dependency footprint, Rust LOC, and the exact reference releases or commits studied.
7. Failure identifies the missing API and a reproducible counterexample; it does not introduce a fork, second terminal engine, or unbounded replay.
notes: Proof result on 2026-08-04: the public formatter path FAILS the exact Orbit attachment contract. The implementation pins crates.io libghostty-vt 0.2.1 with default features and libghostty-vt-sys 0.2.1. Artifact SHA-256 values are 6219ed1c364b3ef5815fb0fd2acc0662f792adc706dabf59b7ca89280ee6d066 and 865fed12a8b2bba3507b3bccd0bef439e06ef1100e652fe6b71d132c41ee8db0. The sys crate pins Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083. The published dependency builds locally with Rust 1.96.0 and Zig 0.15.2. Current libghostty-rs head 72ac98f292879bf9f788fcbb11238c562a1eebe6 has moved to a later Ghostty source requiring Zig 0.16 and was reference evidence only. Tests use one thread as the owner of both !Send and !Sync terminals. The authoritative terminal alone installs on_pty_write; the reconstructed terminal intentionally has no PTY callback, and a DSR query produces exactly one captured response. No other callback is required by the deterministic corpus. Reproducible public-API counterexamples: attaching while alternate is active reconstructs its visible content but loses the inactive primary, so a shared 1049l tail reveals primary text only on the authority; CUP cursor replay loses pending wrap, so the next printable byte diverges; prefixes split inside CSI, four-byte UTF-8, and APC all diverge under a shared suffix because formatter output carries no persistent parser or decoder continuation; full tab-stop replay moves the reconstructed cursor from column 1 to column 4; exact scrollback accounting differs at 5 versus 4 rows even though the checked visible history plus resize tail converges; closed-cell hyperlink URI metadata, OSC title, and Kitty image storage are absent after bootstrap. Checked successes: active text, DECCKM, Kitty keyboard flags, palette, working directory, state-aware Up-key encoding, custom tab behavior after explicit repositioning, charset state, and a currently active hyperlink for future text when tab-stop replay is omitted. Unclassified in this proof: current SGR style, scrolling-region state, and character-protection state; do not infer preservation or loss for them. The public safe binding exposes no inactive-screen formatter, terminal clone, checkpoint, export/import, or serialize/deserialize API. Cargo locks ten third-party crates including the binding, sys crate, and proc-macro stack. By default, the sys crate runs git clone for its pinned Ghostty source when GHOSTTY_SOURCE_DIR is unset and may let Zig resolve packages from the network unless GHOSTTY_ZIG_SYSTEM_DIR supplies a prefetched package set. The local proof build produced an approximately 155 MiB Ghostty source checkout outside owned Rust LOC. Future Nix packaging must prefetch both the Ghostty source and Zig package inputs. Owned Rust is 282 lines: the one-line binary plus 281 test lines. Verification passes cargo fmt --check, cargo check, cargo test with eight contract tests, and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings. References audited: zmx 4f3739ef98f44d0b639afa57fd76bffcad5d0ef4, Ghostling f9034e43a50a2f3a8101e35497f486090c1ddd6e, libghostty-rs 72ac98f292879bf9f788fcbb11238c562a1eebe6, released Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083, and vt100 0.16.2. No fork, binding extension, compatibility wrapper, second terminal engine, bounded or unbounded replay fallback, PTY, socket, or protocol code was added. The decision is not binary: user choices include pursuing an upstream checkpoint/export-import API; changing to structured server-rendered frames; approving a binding extension, fork, or substantial wrapper; comparing another terminal engine; relaxing the exact attachment contract; or stopping the experiment. Bounded raw replay without an exact checkpoint cannot support arbitrarily long sessions while remaining bounded, so it is not a standalone solution to the current contract. The proof stopped at the required decision boundary. User decision after the proof: adopt host-authored structured presentation frames and stop pursuing a reconstructed client terminal plus raw-PTY-tail replication. Orbit retains the sole authoritative libghostty terminal and sole PTY-response callback. A client receives a coherent complete presentation frame followed by ordered frame revisions and sends semantic input for Orbit to encode against authoritative state. The presentation boundary must not become a text-grid ceiling: it must explicitly account for styled cells and graphemes, cursor, title and working directory, hyperlinks, and graphics resources or capabilities. orb-bi4.3 must prove the smallest public read-only extraction surface and stop for another user decision before any binding extension, fork, substantial wrapper, or alternative engine. Full terminal checkpoint export/import, Formatter-as-checkpoint, a second client terminal emulator, and bounded or unbounded raw replay are rejected for the current direction. The initial experiment remains Linux-only, local, one session, and one active client. The long-term contract must not preclude host-owned durable workspace topology or native, web, and mobile clients, but multiple sessions, windows, tabs, splits, remote transport, web, and mobile implementation remain outside the current experiment.
close_reason: Completed: eight contract tests conclusively disprove Formatter checkpoint plus raw-tail replication; dependency and state-loss evidence is recorded, and the user selected sole Orbit terminal authority with host-authored structured presentation frames as the next architecture.

title: Prove PTY lifetime across diagnostic-client disconnect
description: Build the smallest headless Orbit vertical slice that proves process persistence and local transport. Orbit owns one real PTY shell and one authoritative libghostty terminal on a single owner thread. One diagnostic client connects over a local Unix socket. Structured presentation attachment and convergence remain the outcome of orb-bi4.3.
design: Keep one Rust package and binary unless evidence establishes another owner. Use the sole-authority and thread model accepted in orb-bi4.1; do not reconstruct terminal state in the client or establish raw PTY bytes as the client contract. Before proposing a PTY dependency, compare portable-pty with the smallest direct rustix or Linux implementation for lifecycle control, dependency footprint, owned LOC, and testability; study zmx, shpool, abduco, and tastty for concrete process and socket failure behavior. Keep the server in the foreground for the experiment; daemonization policy is deferred. Use a minimal bounded diagnostic message set rather than a general protocol framework. The client sends semantic key, mouse, focus, paste, and resize events; Orbit encodes them against authoritative terminal state and alone owns terminal-generated PTY writes. The active client controls PTY size, and the server retains the last size while detached. Place the socket in a user-private runtime location and define stale-socket cleanup.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A subprocess check starts a real shell, attaches a diagnostic client, exchanges semantic input and diagnostic output, and changes PTY size.
2. Client disconnect leaves the shell and foreground process alive; output produced while detached reaches authoritative server state.
3. A later diagnostic connection reaches the same live PTY. This is a lifecycle smoke test, not presentation-convergence proof.
4. A second simultaneous attach receives one deterministic rejection without disturbing the active client.
5. Child exit, server shutdown, signal handling, process reaping, socket permissions, and stale-socket cleanup have explicit checked behavior.
6. Checks use observable synchronization and bounded timeouts rather than sleep as a correctness mechanism.
7. The result records the zmx, shpool, abduco, tastty, portable-pty, and rustix releases or commits inspected, the lifecycle lessons used, and why the selected PTY level is smaller for this contract.
8. Focused checks verify that Orbit, not the client, performs state-aware key and mouse encoding and owns focus and paste encoding; this does not create a general input protocol.
9. A pre-implementation, append-only `Reference gate` comment satisfies AGENTS.md before the first implementation edit, and closure evidence satisfies the AGENTS.md closure gate.
notes:
Current candidate evidence (2026-08-04):
- Protocol state: comments 22 and 23 record this run's execution baseline and reference gate before its test edit. The user then clarified AGENTS.md so future read-only review happens before run comments and the gates begin only after a concrete edit candidate exists. The existing append-only comments remain factual. This run did not invoke or extend the one-time retroactive exception for the original candidate.
- Ownership and scope: one foreground Linux process, package, binary, and owner thread own one real PTY child, one nonblocking master, one libghostty-vt terminal, one private Unix listener, and at most one bounded diagnostic client. No raw PTY attachment, presentation frame, daemon, library split, general protocol, module, dependency, feature, contract, or planning bead was added.
- Contract routing: ORB-C1 and ORB-C2 were inspected for regressions; ORB-C3 and ORB-C5 remain observably preserved. ORB-C4, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 remain outside this bead. All affected contracts remain Partially proved until the user accepts and authorizes an immutable proof-bearing commit.
- Exact references inspected across the candidate and fresh-eyes runs: libghostty-vt/sys 0.2.1 and pinned Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083; zmx 4f3739ef98f44d0b639afa57fd76bffcad5d0ef4; shpool 901e18c3ced010073178b78c0ca2a8cdd43e8581; abduco 8c32909a159aaa9484c82b71f05b7a73321eb491; tastty 0.1.1; portable-pty 0.9.0; rustix 1.1.4; rustix-openpty 0.2.0; comparison-only nix 0.31.3; and Rust 1.96 standard-library Child, Command, and SIGPIPE behavior.
- Crate decision: retain direct libc 0.2.189 for the candidate. Nix still needs explicit CLOEXEC and ioctl work and has no demonstrated net owned-LOC reduction; rustix-openpty adds layers and packages; portable-pty imposes a broader ownership model. The normal dependency graph is unchanged, and the fresh-eyes runs did not edit Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock.
- Confirmed production regressions fixed in prior passes: final child PTY output reaches authoritative libghostty state before exit publication; startup signal cleanup owns the socket; aborted ATTACHED writes cannot terminate Orbit; shutdown reaps a distinct foreground process group; and SocketGuard does not remove a later socket identity.
- Confirmed test omission fixed in this pass: lifecycle tests held raw std::process::Child values. Rust 1.96 explicitly provides no Child Drop cleanup, so any assertion or ? failure before an explicit wait could leak Orbit and its PTY process. A bounded Server guard now requests the normal SIGTERM path and waits on scope exit. Explicit shutdown tests share the same shutdown method.
- Isomorphic test simplification: the diagnostic test client writes through the UnixStream already owned by BufReader, removing a duplicate descriptor, clone-failure path, and no-op UnixStream flush. Request/response order, socket timeouts, buffered reads, protocol bytes, error assertions, and product behavior remain unchanged.
- Rejected concern: Linux accepted sockets do not inherit listener nonblocking, but Orbit performs one read only after poll readiness, so no second blocking drain read exists. Blocking client output and fairness belong to ORB-C7.
- Rejected simplifications: no parser/protocol rewrite, cross-platform trait or physical platform module before orb-pmp, new crate, weaker lifecycle/security checks, production stream-ownership change with different public failure semantics, ORB-C7 buffering/backpressure work, or background-process-tree guarantee. These change behavior, broaden scope, or fail the measured architecture/verification threshold.
- Contract checks: 13 tests cover authoritative semantic input, final PTY output drain, formatter counterexamples, real-shell resize, same-PID detach/reattach, detached output, deterministic BUSY rejection, aborted attach recovery, private runtime/socket permissions, stale and replacement socket behavior, normal child exit, startup/established SIGTERM cleanup, and foreground process reaping.
- Verification: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked (13 passed); cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check. The lifecycle test binary passed 250 consecutive concurrent direct runs after this pass.
- Owned Rust LOC: 1,486 total: 847 src/main.rs, 281 formatter proof, and 358 lifecycle tests. Unsafe-bearing lines remain 17 in source and 3 in tests. The 16-line increase is bounded failure-path cleanup in the lifecycle harness; production code is unchanged in this pass.
- Portability disposition: isolated platform dependency. Linux-specific PTY, process-group, signal, poll, fd, socket-permission, and EIO mechanics remain explicit functions; terminal authority and semantic input do not depend on them. orb-pmp owns the physical platform-seam decision before orb-bi4.3.
- Remaining limitations: Linux, one session/client, a tiny diagnostic protocol, no restart persistence, presentation frame, convergence proof, slow-client/backpressure hardening, general input API, renderer, or background-process-tree guarantee. orb-bi4.2 remains in_progress and uncommitted pending user acceptance and authorization of a proof-bearing commit.

Acceptance and closure (2026-08-04): the user authorized commit and push. The immutable proof-bearing revision is ac0a291ebe7fcebe4d7cace914b89363856c4903. ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C3, and ORB-C5 are Proved at that revision; ORB-C4, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 remain outside this bead. Direct libc 0.2.189 is selected for the Linux experiment under the recorded retroactive crate gate, with orb-pmp retaining the platform-seam decision. CHANGELOG.md records the accepted runtime behavior. The exact proof revision passed cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked (13 passed); cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; and git diff --check before commit.

Contracts affected: ORB-C1 and ORB-C2 are corrected/hardened; ORB-C3 and ORB-C5 must remain observably unchanged. Required identities inspected: libghostty-vt 0.2.1 with pinned Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083; zmx 4f3739ef98f44d0b639afa57fd76bffcad5d0ef4; shpool 901e18c3ced010073178b78c0ca2a8cdd43e8581; abduco 8c32909a159aaa9484c82b71f05b7a73321eb491; tastty 0.1.1 crates.io source; portable-pty 0.9.0; rustix 1.1.4; rustix-openpty 0.2.0. title: Prove atomic structured presentation convergence on reattach
description: Implement the defining Orbit attachment contract on the real PTY slice: Orbit remains the sole authoritative libghostty terminal, and an attaching client receives one coherent complete host-authored presentation frame followed by ordered frame revisions. The client never reconstructs terminal authority from Formatter output or raw PTY bytes.
design: Use the authority and lifecycle model proven in orb-bi4.1 and orb-bi4.2. First determine the smallest public read-only libghostty surface that can produce a structured presentation frame; study Ghostling, libghostty-rs, and justerm-core at recorded revisions. Formatter output may be evidence but is not a checkpoint or client protocol. Serialize PTY reads, authoritative terminal mutation, frame extraction, and publication through one owner so attachment has no race window. Start with complete coalesced frames carrying a monotonic revision rather than premature deltas. The representation must not silently flatten the terminal to plain text: account explicitly for dimensions, styled cells and graphemes, cursor, active screen, title and working directory, hyperlinks, and graphics resources or declared capabilities. Hidden terminal state such as inactive screens, pending wrap, parser continuation, scrollback semantics, and terminal-generated responses stays exclusively in Orbit; later frames must reflect its visible consequences. The client sends semantic input and never runs a second terminal emulator or answers the PTY. Keep the initial protocol local, one-session, one-client, and bounded. It may leave workspace topology and remote transport for later while avoiding a text-grid-only architectural ceiling. If the public API cannot expose the minimum presentation state, record the exact missing read-only API and stop for user choice before a binding extension, fork, substantial wrapper, or alternative engine.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A real PTY establishes authoritative terminal state, emits output while detached, and continues output while a client attaches.
2. The first attach message is one coherent complete presentation frame at revision N; output racing attachment is reflected either in that frame or a later strictly ordered revision, with no duplicate revision or stale final state.
3. The checked presentation corpus covers styled text, Unicode and graphemes, cursor state, active and alternate screens, title, working directory, hyperlinks, and graphics capability or resource handling; unsupported state is explicit rather than silently discarded.
4. Counterexamples from orb-bi4.1—an inactive primary screen, pending wrap, and parser splits inside CSI, UTF-8, and APC or graphics input—remain correct because their hidden state stays in Orbit and their later visible effects appear in subsequent frames.
5. Varying PTY read chunk boundaries and attaching during output does not change the eventual authoritative presentation.
